title: A Java class can exist without methods or fields
answer: Yes. A Java class can legally declare no fields and no methods. The compiler still creates a class type, and if no constructor is declared, it provides a default no-argument constructor when allowed by the class definition. Such empty classes can be used as marker types, placeholders, test fixtures, or simple type tokens, although marker annotations are often clearer for metadata-style use cases. An empty class still implicitly extends `Object` unless another superclass is specified.
